summary: Bokondini Airport (BUI) is a small highland airstrip serving the remote Lanny Jaya Regency in the mountainous interior of Papua, Indonesia. The airport provides a vital air link for the local Dani and Lani peoples living in one of the most isolated regions of the country. Its short runway nestled among jungle-covered ridges makes it an important but challenging gateway to the central Papuan highlands.
faqs:
Q: Where is Bokondini Airport located?
A: It is situated in the Lanny Jaya Regency of Papua, Indonesia, in the central highland region of the island.

Q: What airlines serve Bokondini Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by small regional carriers operating turboprop aircraft on domestic Papua routes.

Q: Is Bokondini Airport suitable for large aircraft?
A: No, it has a short runway suitable only for small STOL (Short Take-Off and Landing) aircraft common in Papua.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: Facilities are minimal, typical of remote Papua airstrips, with basic terminal services and limited amenities.
transport_tips: Getting to and from Bokondini Airport usually requires a short ride by local transport arranged in advance, as taxi services are informal and limited. The town center is within a short drive of the airstrip. Travelers should expect rough road conditions and plan for flexible pickup timing, as flights can be delayed by weather.
local_tip: Bring warm clothing and rain gear year-round, as Bokondini sits at high elevation in the central highlands where temperatures drop noticeably at night and afternoon rain is common.
